question: How should the Cairn Hermes adapter own bounded recall and synchronous selected capture across CLI and Slack gateway session lifecycle without changing Hermes core?
scope: Native interactive Hermes CLI and configured Slack gateway adapter mechanics; deployment authorized by owner

authority_boundary.authority_source: Owner goal: complete the hermes integration according to the plan then deploy; initial scope explicitly CLI and messaging gateways.
authorized_scope: Implement, verify, land and deploy the Hermes integration
Preserve native memory and unrelated host configuration; no real Slack test messages

evidence.summary: This is an additive interactive adapter, not a behavior-preserving refactor. User requested completing and deploying both surfaces. No change leaves Hermes without automatic Cairn memory. MCP-only offers explicit tools but cannot meet that request; generic hooks alone miss the proven native pre-compression callback. The provider reuses existing selection policy, occupies one external-provider slot, adds synchronous model latency and cannot guarantee capture after abrupt death. Installer preserves native files/configuration values, backups and uninstall; native probes verify timeout, label isolation, retry, correction and no sidecar echo. Cairn API/PostgreSQL/owned adapter are managed and run as real disposable components; externally operated model inference and Slack delivery are substituted at those external boundaries only. Other agents observe versioned notes through authenticated Cairn API, not fixture database tables. Shared engine edits are two compatibility additions (Hermes label/hash and bare-resume project anchor); existing native Claude/OpenCode regression passes. Test-helper repo argument only parameterizes the same fixture behavior. Supporting installer, tests and documentation implement the requested slice. The design does not introduce a new dependency-inversion abstraction or claim net economic benefit.

evidence.summary: Final installed-Hermes native fixture passed against disposable PostgreSQL and real Cairn/Claude processes with scripted model endpoints and captured Slack transport. CLI and real GatewayRunner/Slack parsing discover ordinary tools, search/pull/create/revise notes, inject bounded request context, save selected decisions/checkpoints, correct existing records and continue across agents. Manual CLI/gateway compression and native compressor path pass. Duplicate delivery, concurrent chats, same-label context-local profiles, reset, expiry, simulated transport reconnect, runner restart, stale switch callbacks and interrupted shutdown pass. Two actual 35-second selector timeouts preserve task completion and retry after recovery. Unit tests kill the entire hung subprocess group and check per-instance registration cleanup and opt-out buffer discard. Original dialogue excludes tool results, reasoning, recalled sidecars and native memory. 97 fixture requests, 17 selector calls; 19 successful recall operations take 43-99ms; fixture-only latency is not production inference cost. Actual Slack network delivery and long-term task benefit are outside this verification claim.

evidence.summary: Existing shared lifecycle engine owns bounded relevance, selected extraction, current-record revision and digest confirmation; Hermes provider translates actual lifecycle labels and original dialogue. Cairn calls have five-second deadlines, selector 35 seconds, complete adapter process group 150 seconds. Results require successful exit and JSON object; diagnostics omit raw subprocess content. Errors leave pending capture retryable. Only provider registers per-instance callbacks; request middleware appends at most 12000 bytes without editing persisted sidecars. Each instance has a lock, bounded original dialogue (24000 bytes) and 32 labels. Native MCP scope is profile-level, automatic operations session-labelled, neither is authentication. API refusal and unavailable socket, selector hangs, malformed engine output and outer process-group timeout are covered in shared/focused/native tests.
